records.label: Neutral theory of molecular evolution

changed_fields_review.before: The neutral theory of molecular evolution emphasizes mutations and genetic drift in explaining much genetic variation. If alternative versions have similar effects on reproductive success, chance can change their frequencies. This does not mean all variation is neutral or that natural selection is unimportant.
changed_fields_review.after: The neutral theory of molecular evolution emphasizes mutation and genetic drift in explaining much genetic variation. When alternative gene versions do not differ in fitness, chance can change their frequencies. This does not mean all variation is neutral or that natural selection is unimportant.
changed_fields_review.assessment: Pass: replacing similar reproductive effects with no fitness difference restores the source’s neutral condition. Mutation/drift emphasis and selection caveats remain supported.

changed_fields_review.before: Berkeley states the theory’s emphasis on mutation/drift and explicitly rejects the three overgeneralizations about all variation and the importance of selection.
changed_fields_review.after: Berkeley emphasizes mutation and drift and defines the illustrative neutral alternatives as having no difference in fitness. It explicitly rejects claims that all variation is neutral or selection is unimportant.
changed_fields_review.assessment: Pass: revised evidence note accurately attributes the no-difference example and limits.

changed_fields_review.before: Neutral theory assigns a major explanatory role to genetic drift for variation with little fitness effect, rather than introducing a different drift mechanism.
changed_fields_review.after: Neutral theory assigns a major explanatory role to genetic drift for variants with no fitness difference, rather than introducing a different drift mechanism.
changed_fields_review.assessment: Pass: the changed relation rationale uses the same no-fitness-difference premise; genetic drift remains the same chance mechanism. Q486420 resolves to that baseline meaning.

records.label: Marine heatwave

changed_fields_review.before: A marine heatwave is unusually warm ocean water measured against the normal conditions for that place and season. A common definition requires temperatures above the seasonal ninetieth percentile for at least five days. The comparison is local and time-specific, not one temperature threshold for every sea.
changed_fields_review.after: A marine heatwave is unusually warm ocean water measured against the normal conditions for that place and season. A common definition requires temperatures above the seasonal ninetieth percentile for at least five consecutive days. The comparison is local and time-specific, not one temperature threshold for every sea.
changed_fields_review.assessment: Pass: consecutive preserves the uninterrupted-duration requirement; the local seasonal threshold and common-definition qualification are supported.

records.label: Temperature inversion

changed_fields_review.before: During a temperature inversion, warmer air lies above cooler air near the ground. This stable arrangement can suppress mixing and trap pollutants in the lower atmosphere. Inversions may form through nighttime surface cooling or the arrival of warmer air above an existing cool layer.
changed_fields_review.after: A temperature inversion occurs where air becomes warmer with height. Near the ground, warm air above cooler air can suppress mixing and trap pollution. Such inversions may form through nighttime surface cooling or warm-air advection above an existing cool layer.
changed_fields_review.assessment: Pass: definition now covers any increasing-temperature-with-height layer; near-ground formation and pollution effects are correctly presented as examples.

changed_fields_review.after: NWS defines an inversion as air temperature increasing with height. Its near-ground examples describe nighttime surface cooling or warm-air advection, with a stable lid that can trap pollution.

records.label: Rootstock dwarfing

changed_fields_review.before: A dwarfing rootstock can keep an apple tree smaller even when its scion belongs to a familiar full-size fruit variety. The two parts have different jobs. changed_fields_review.assessment: Pass: scion fruit-variety role and rootstock size influence are correctly separated; scion rooting and loss of dwarfing are supported.

records.label: Wood sorption hysteresis

changed_fields_review.before: Wood’s moisture content can depend on whether it approached a humidity level by drying or by absorbing water. changed_fields_review.after: Wood’s equilibrium moisture content can depend on whether it reached a humidity level by drying or by absorbing water. At the same temperature and relative humidity, the drying path can retain more moisture. This sorption hysteresis makes moisture history relevant even after equilibrium is reached.
changed_fields_review.assessment: Pass: equilibrium and equal temperature/RH now delimit the comparison; higher moisture on desorption and path dependence at equilibrium are explicitly supported.
